B. BF₃ (Boron trifluoride):
- B has an electronegativity of about 2.0

- The electronegativity difference is approximately 2.0
- This difference is in the range where the bond is considered polar covalent
- BF₃ has significant ionic character in its bonds

C. CH₄ (Methane):

- The electronegativity difference is approximately 0.4
- This small difference makes the C-H bonds predominantly non-polar covalent

D. NaHg (Sodium amalgam):

- This is a metallic alloy with predominantly metallic bonding
- It has ionic character as well

E. S₈ (Cyclic sulfur):
- S-S bonds are between the same element
- The electronegativity difference is 0
- Bonds between identical atoms are always non-polar covalent
